description: Photograph taken from behind a man with distinctive blond-orange hair, consistent with President Donald Trump, seen entering or standing in the crowded U.S. House of Representatives chamber. The engraved motto IN GOD WE TRUST appears above the rostrum with an American flag hanging beneath it, in the manner of a State of the Union address. Surrounding figures in suits applaud and reach in to shake hands.
flags: Central figure seen only from behind; identified as Trump from hair and House-chamber context, not his face

description: Screenshot of a verified tweet by Ian Miles Cheong (@stillgray) claiming George Soros is the single largest donor of Shadow Inc., the company behind the failed 2020 Iowa Caucus app. Attached is a Datawrapper donor table credited to Alex Kotch of Sludge, sourced to IRS data, listing Soros at $2,600,000 atop eleven other donors. The table itself does not name Shadow Inc.; the Soros-to-Shadow link is the tweet's claim.
text: Ian Miles Cheong @stillgray. And there it is. The single largest donor of Shadow Inc., the company behind the failed Iowa Caucus app, is George Soros. Donor. Employer/Job. Amount. George Soros. Soros Fund Management. $2,600,000. Fred Eychaner. Newsweb Corporation. $1,500,000. United Food And Commercial Workers Union ABC. $1,350,000. AFSCME. $572,105. S. Donald Sussman. Paloma Partners. $500,000. James C. Hormel. Equidex. $300,000. Air Line Pilots Association PAC. $300,000. Martha S. Samuelson. Analysis Group. $275,000. SEIU COPE. $200,000. Jon Stryker. Architect. $200,000. Donald Mullen, Jr. Pretium Partners. $200,000. Anne G. Earhart. Investor. $200,000. Table: Alex Kotch, Sludge • Source: Internal Revenue Service • Get the data • Created with Datawrapper
orgs: United Food And Commercial Workers Union
flags: The tweet's claim that these are Shadow Inc. donors is disputed; contemporaneous reporting tied the listed donations to the affiliated PAC (Pacronym/ACRONYM), not directly to Shadow Inc.
Tweet screenshot lacks a visible date/timestamp; filename dates it around 2020-02-05

description: Photograph of the Democratic side of the U.S. House chamber during the February 2020 State of the Union address, with rows of congresswomen dressed in suffragette white looking bored, weary, or displeased; one reads a folded pamphlet. In the front row sit Reps. Adam Schiff, Jerrold Nadler, Zoe Lofgren, and Hakeem Jeffries — the House impeachment-era leadership — in dark suits. The archive filename frames the scene as a question about patriotism versus contempt.
flags: Event and date inferred from the white attire and visible members; not printed in the image
Other congresswomen present are left unnamed rather than guessed from faces
